meta.title: Clay & Paper — why subscribers leave in month three
meta.description: Research readout for a monthly pottery-kit subscription: three findings on month-three churn, the method, evidence for each finding, a subscriber's voice, what surprised us, limits, ranked recommendations and the decision needed.

slides.heading: Subscribers leave in month three because kits repeat, not price.
slides.lead: Findings from 1,284 survey answers, 36 interviews and 18 months of orders.
slides.notes: This is a readout, not a pitch. Lead with the finding and let the evidence carry it.

slides.heading: Three findings explain most of the month-three drop

cards.title: Repeats push people out
cards.body: A repeated technique triples next-month cancellations.

cards.title: Finishing early keeps them
cards.body: Subscribers who finish in week one stay 11.4 months.

cards.title: Price matters less
cards.body: Only 14% of leavers name price as a reason.

slides.heading: Month three loses 31% of each cohort and $1.4M a year
slides.lead: Other months lose 6–9%. The gap costs 418 subscribers a month. What makes month three different?

slides.heading: What we found
slides.lead: Three findings, each with its evidence.

slides.heading: A repeated technique triples next-month cancellations to 24%
slides.lead: Source: order data, 22,800 subscribers, Jan 2025–Jun 2026. Repeat = same core technique as an earlier kit.

slides.quote: The third box was another pinch pot. I'd already made four of them.
slides.by: Interview 14, UK subscriber, cancelled in month three

slides.heading: Subscribers who finish in week one stay 11.4 months, not 3.1
columns: When the first kit is finished

slides.heading: Price is fourth among reasons to cancel, named by 14%
slides.lead: Share of 1,284 leavers naming each reason; more than one allowed.

slides.heading: We expected price to drive churn; repetition and time did
slides.left:
Leavers find $34 a month too much.
A discount in month three saves them.
slides.right:
Leavers want a new skill each month.
A 15% discount test saved 2 points of churn; repeats cost 16.
slides.notes: Own the wrong guess. We ran the discount test in Q2 before this study; it is why we looked further.

slides.heading: What we should do
slides.lead: How sure we are, then three moves in order.

slides.heading: Confidence is high for UK subscribers and medium for the US
rows: US is 30% of the base but 44% of interviews
US time pressure may be overstated

slides.heading: Fix the kit sequence first; it reaches 46% of leavers
Approve a no-repeat kit plan before the March box ships
slides.lead: Kits repeat, not price. If we act by 15 January, the March cohort gets the new sequence.
